I am seventy years old, never went to school for even one day. I only started handling my own land last year — before that, my younger brother farmed it, but he moved to the city to live with his son. I have six mu total. The four mu by the road, I do wheat in the cold season and maize right after the wheat comes off. The one mu near the ditch is cotton. The last mu, my daughter-in-law heard that stevia leaves sell for good money, so we tried it last year and I will plant it again.

I don't read books and I don't trust outside talk. I watch Old Zhang across the road and the others. Whatever fertilizer bags they carry from the shop, I buy the same. Last year for wheat, I put one big bag of compound fertilizer on each mu — that's fifty jin per mu — and then spread another half bag of urea when the wheat was jointing. The wheat gave me about nine hundred jin from the four mu. This year I will do the same: one bag compound fertilizer first, half bag urea later. I irrigate three times — before winter, at jointing, and when the heads come out. I spray twice for bugs and weeds. I buy the improved wheat seeds from the seed shop, the ones in the red bags that everyone uses.

For maize, after we cut the wheat I hire the machine to plant right away. No deep ploughing, the machine just opens the soil and drops the seeds — fast, so we don't miss the season. I put about forty jin of compound fertilizer per mu, then spread twenty jin of urea when the plants are knee-high. Irrigate twice, spray twice. The seeds are hybrid, everyone uses hybrid now, they grow thick and the cobs are heavy. Last year I got about two thousand jin from the four mu.

Cotton needs more work. I plough that field deep because cotton roots like loose soil. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, and add urea two more times. I irrigate three times and spray four times — the red spiders and bollworms always come. I hope for two hundred jin of seed cotton per mu.

Stevia, I am still learning. Last year I put about forty jin of compound fertilizer, irrigated three times, sprayed twice. It made about two hundred jin of dried leaves per mu. This year I will do exactly the same. No point changing what worked.

I always say: better the crop gets fat than goes hungry. Fertilizer costs money, yes, but if the harvest fails, my family loses real money. My son and daughter-in-law work in the county factory and send some wages back, but we have seven mouths to feed. I would rather spend a few more yuan on fertilizer than take a risk.
